texts.preamble: Gangamma C vs Deekshith M on 12 November, 2025 Scch-26 M.V.C.No.7730/2023 Kabc020377002023 Before The Court Of Xxiv Additional Small Causes Judge And The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal & A.C.J.M. (Scch-26) At: Bengaluru. Dated This The 12th Day Of November 2025 Present: Sri. Appasab Naik, B.A.L.L.B.(Spl) Xxiv Addl. Scj & Acjm & Member-Mact Bengaluru. M.V.C No.7730/2023 Petitioner : Gangamma C., W/o Yerappa, D/o Chittappa, Aged about 24 years, Residing at No.7-11-A, M. Rayapuram Village and Post, Rolla Mandalam, Ananthapuram District, Andhra Pradesh-515271. Also at: Shakthivelu Building, No.42/2, Devinagara, Bhadrappa Layout, Bangalore-560 092. (By Sri. N.R. Shivanna- Advocate) V/ s. Respondents 1. Deekshith M., S/o Mohan L., Scch - 26 2 M.V.C.No.7730/2023 No.58-59, Pipe Line Road, Prashanth Nagar, T. Dasarahalli, Bangalore North, Bangalore-560 057. (R.C. Owner of Ktm Avenger-250 Motor Gangamma C vs Deekshith M on 12 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57391937/ 1 Cycle bearing Reg.No. Ka-04-Kl-8554) (By Sri. C.R. Venkatesh-Advocate) 2. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Regional Office, #9/2, Mahalakshmi Chambers, M.G. Road, Bengaluru-560 001. (Policy No.67140131220900003950, Valid from 31.01.2023 to 30.01.2028). (By Sri. K.B.Mallikarjuna-Advocate) :: Judgment:
texts.facts: : The petition is filed by the petitioner under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 seeking to award compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by her in the road traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under: On 17.11.2023 at about 6.50 am., the petitioner was standing on the extreme left side of Devinagara Cross Bus SCCH - 26 3 M.V.C.No.7730/2023 Stop, Bhadrappa Layout, situated on Ring Road for waiting the bus in order to go to her duty at Manipal Hospital, Yeshwanthapura. At that time, the rider of KTM Avenger- 250 Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-KL-8554 suddenly came from Hebbal towards B.E.L. side in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, without observing any of the traffic rules and dashed against the petitioner. Due to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body. 3. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein X-rays were taken, which reveals abrasion over the face, mild swelling right maxillary region, left knee swelling present on lateral aspect, severe injuries to hand, legs. The petitioner was treated with analgesics and dressing was done and discharged. Due to severe pain, the petitioner once again taken treatment in the aforesaid hospital as an inpatient from 20.11.2023 to 22.11.2023, MRI was done, which shows left knee lateral condyle depressed fracture, for which she has undergone surgery on 21.11.2023. The petitioner SCCH - 26 4 M.V.C.No.7730/2023 was discharged with an advise to take follow-up treatment, restricted fracture movements and complete bed rest with suitable exercises. Petitioner has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges. Gangamma C vs Deekshith M on 12 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57391937/ 2 4. The injuries sustained by the petitioner was not recovered, she is getting unbearable pain, headache, giddiness, she cannot walk stand, sit, squat on floor, use Indian type of toilet, carry weight, cannot chew hard food. There are scar marks present over the face, due to which the petitioner looking ugly and she is suffering from pain and the injuries caused to her are permanent in nature. Further submitted that prior to the accident petitioner was hale and healthy, she was working as a Nurse at Manipal Hospital, Yeshwanthapur, Bengaluru and she was earning Rs.28,000/- p.m. She was maintained her family members, since she is the only earning member in the family. Due to accidental injuries, the petitioner cannot attend to her work which resulted the loss of earning, earning capacity and she put to great financial hardship. SCCH - 26 5 M.V.C.No.7730/2023 5. The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the KTM Avenger-250 Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-KL-8554 by its rider and in this connection, the Hebbal Traffic Police have registered the case in Cr.No.214/2023 and filed charge sheet punishable under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC against the said rider. At the time of accident, the first respondent being the R.C owner of the aforesaid KTM Avenger-250 motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 04-KL-8554 and the 2nd respondent being the insurer, the policy was in force as on the date of accident. Hence both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation. Accordingly, the petitioner has prayed to award compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- together with cost and interest. 6. After service of summons, Respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared through their respective counsels and filed objection statements. 7. Respondent No.1-R.C. owner of the offending vehicle has filed objection by denying the entire petition averments. SCCH - 26 6 M.V.C.No.7730/2023 He has denied the rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle by its rider, injuries and disability sustained by the petitioner, treatment taken by her and amount spent towards treatment. Further denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner. For all these, he has prayed to dismiss the petition. 8. Respondent No.2 - Insurer of Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-KL-8554 has filed objection contending that, SCCH - 26 7 M.V.C.No.7730/2023 the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts. Further contended that, the accident was occurred on 17.11.2923, but it was reported to police on 19.11.2023 i.e., after delay of 2 days and it appears that, the offending motor cycle was falsely implicated to the accident only to get compensation. 10. In order to prove her case, the petitioner herself examined as PW.1 and got marked 30 documents as per Ex.P.1 to 30. She has examined Dr. Nagaraj B.N., as PW.2 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.P.31 and Ex.P.32.
texts.arguments: He has contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and unreasonable without any legal basis. Further contended that, petitioner was not followed the rules and the accident was took place due to her fault, not for the fault of the driver of 1st respondent, but the said fact was suppressed by the petitioner and filed false case only to grab the money. Further contended that, in the accident place heavy vehicles are moving and it is the busy road, hence it shows that, due to negligence of the petitioner the accident was happened. Further contended that, at the time of accident, insurance policy was valid, hence the 2nd respondent is responsible to pay compensation. This respondent has admitted the Gangamma C vs Deekshith M on 12 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57391937/ 3 issuance of insurance policy with respect to offending vehicle and contended that, the liability if any is subject to validity of RC, FC and driving licence of the rider of above said vehicle. Further contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant. This respondent has denied all the allegations made in the petition. Further denied the rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle by its rider, injuries sustained by the petition, treatment taken and amount spent by her towards treatment, age, occupation and income of the petitioner. It is contended that, the petitioner had to wait for the bus at the bus shelter on the footpath provided for the safety of the commuters, but she had stepped down on the road and thereby she has violated the traffic rules, hence the accident SCCH - 26 8 M.V.C.No.7730/2023 was occurred due to own negligence of the petitioner. Without proper investigation the police have registered the case against the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04- KL-8554 to help the petitioner only to get compensation. The owner of the alleged offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act. The rider of offending vehicle had no valid driving licence to ride the same as on the date of accident, which is clear violation of terms and conditions of the policy. Hence this respondent is not liable to pay compensation. For all these, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition. At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants. Again it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2003 Karnataka page 493, between Mallamma Vs. Balaji and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held at para 12 as hereunder: " Filing of the charge sheet against the driver is also a prima-facie case to hold SCCH - 26 11 M.V.C.No.7730/2023 that, the driver of the said lorry was responsible for the accident and burden shifts on him to proves the same". 14. On the other hand, the advocate for the petitioner vehemently argued that the evidence of PW-2 speaks that the petitioner is suffering from physical permanent disability of 13% to the whole body. The petitioner became a disabled and unable to do her work as she was working prior to the accident and sustained loss of her future earnings. In the absence of material documents it is difficult to prove that she was working as nurse prior to the accident. Therefore the petitioner do not produced any evidence to show that due to the injuries sustained in the accident, she is sustained loss of her future earnings.
